overview: Black counter-attacks the d4 pawn at once. After 3.dxe5 Ng4 Black develops quickly and usually regains the e5 pawn with ...Nc6 and ...Bb4+ or ...Ngxe5. The play is open and forcing, with Black accepting a slightly worse structure for activity. 3.d5 and 3.e3 avoid the complications.

white_ideas.idea: Hold the extra pawn with Bf4, Nf3 and Nbd2 or e3, then play for a small edge

black_ideas.idea: Regain e5 with ...Nc6, ...Bb4+ and ...Qe7, then use the knight pair and development
Trap White with early tactics against Bf4 or e5

typical_structures.structure: White c4/e3 centre against Black pieces active on e5 and c5, open centre

character.notes: Concrete and forcing in the Adler and Fajarowicz lines; Black has to know the traps.

gambit.notes: Black normally regains e5 by force after 3.dxe5 Ng4 4.Bf4 Nc6 5.Nf3 Bb4+, so it is not a true gambit.

soundness.notes: A rarely used reply but not refuted, small White edge.

structure.notes: Centre opens after dxe5 with active pieces; Open.

approach.notes: Strong players seldom pick it, though it is not an offbeat joke; standard.

level.notes: Needs knowing the traps and Adler/Rubinstein lines but plans are clear.

sublines_that_differ.name: Fajarowicz
sublines_that_differ.how: Black gambits a pawn, more speculative.

character.reason: Open, forcing play with early traps.

gambit.reason: Black usually regains the pawn by force.

soundness.reason: Playable though White keeps a small edge.

structure.reason: e5 and centre pawns come off, giving open lines.

approach.reason: Rare but still an occasional choice for strong players.

level.reason: Traps and the Adler line need learning.

plans.reason: Black seeks active pieces for the e5 pawn.
